reason: Each child glosses a verse line on which faculties are necessarily possessed and argues it, with objections raised and answered (e.g. on the mindless absorptions).
Two children each gloss one verse line giving the minimum count of faculties for two cases.
Two children each gloss one verse line giving the maximum count of faculties for ordinary beings and noble ones.
Three children each gloss one line stating that atoms arise with eight, nine or ten substances.
The children define each mental factor of the five great classes in detail and the last discusses the indeterminate factors and answers objections about their number.
The children list how many mental factors accompany virtuous, non-virtuous and neutral desire-realm minds, each a count with its constituent classes.
Two children each gloss a verse line naming which mental factors are absent in the first dhyana and above.
Two children briefly define affection and respect and state the realms where they occur.
Two children give short glosses: mind, mentation and consciousness as synonyms, and the synonyms of concomitants with the five equalities.
The second child discusses acquisition of the cessations at length and records the Vaibhasika-Vasubandhu dispute over whether acquisition is substantial.
The children analyse the features of acquisition and non-acquisition at length, with sub-points, scriptural citations, doubts and the infinite-regress debate.
The children identify asamjnika, its fruit and level, and the last raises and answers a doubt and records the master's dissenting view.
The children explain the attainment of non-perception and the attainment of cessation at length, including the Kashmiri debate on the bodhisattva's attainment.
Each child raises and resolves a distinct objection about the characteristics of the conditioned (infinite regress, over-extension).
The children explain features of the name/phrase/letter groups, including a Kar-tik dispute and a long quotation from Rajaputra on the Buddha's speech.
The second child analyses the ten ways concomitants follow mind in detail, with qualifications and reasons.
The children explain the homogeneous cause, the third analysing the uncontaminated path across nine levels with a doubt answered.
The children explain each of the five results with arguments, definitions, citations and tetralemmas.
The children analyse when causes grasp and yield results, with reasoning and a discussion of the Sanskrit prefix and a proposed retranslation.
The children are an explanation-and-summary split: one verse gloss of which causes produce which dharmas and a one-line summary.
The children explain the four conditions with definitions, objections and a debate between Vaibhasika, Jam-sgeg and the Kar-tik.
Three children each gloss one verse line on the time at which given causes and conditions act.
Three children each gloss one verse line stating which dharmas arise from four, three or two conditions.
Four children each gloss one verse line on how elements and derived matter act as causes of each other.
Two children each list which minds follow and precede a virtuous desire-realm mind.
Two children each list which minds follow and precede a non-virtuous desire-realm mind.
Two children each list which minds follow and precede obscured and unobscured neutral desire-realm minds.
Two children each list which minds follow and precede a virtuous form-realm mind.
Two children each list which minds follow and precede obscured and unobscured neutral form-realm minds.
Two children each list which minds follow and precede a virtuous formless-realm mind.
Three children each list how many kinds of mind are obtained when a defiled mind of each realm arises.
Two children gloss the desire realm's six destinies with brief etymologies and list its twenty divisions.
Two children each gloss one verse line on the three-fold and eight-fold divisions of the form-realm dhyana levels.
The children explain the formless realm, including how its four spheres are named from meditative practice and a doubt answered on what the mind-stream rests on.
The children identify the seven stations of consciousness and in one line the realms that are not stations.
The children identify the nine abodes of beings and in one line why the lower destinies are excluded.
The children identify the four stations as the four contaminated aggregates and in one line exclude consciousness itself.
Three children each gloss one verse line naming which modes of birth occur in which destinies, with brief examples.
